items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: We played together too. ... he played lots of jobs with our band.

ctx.x: Bill and him took part. I got the picture in there right now. Jolly boy, I don't know about that chair. That's the Sunday we lost. George Lewis fell out. He was working with John. I don't even know who the band he was. I think he was working with John. He was in Two Clown. I was with the Eureka band working at Alfred William's place. Alfred suffered with his heart and he couldn't make that level. It was a hot Sunday in August. Last Sunday in August. Temperature was 90. And hot sunny, snow clouds. Hot is scorching…
That was his funeral, was it?

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: Now that band that consisted of during them times, Red Island on Trump and Henry Red Island on cornet... and I was on the drum.

ctx.x: And the Pack House that was located on the court had the restaurant and ball and pool table downstairs. They called it, they was run by this fella by the name of Faubacher. And this fella, Bebe, William Ridgely's brother, he was the manager of the place. I think I don't know, remember his name? His first name? Yeah, his first name was Bebe Ridgely, his first name, he was a big tall, brown skin, heavy built man. But he was the manager of that place there, I can't think of his first name. But all I can tell you,…
What's the name of that band?
